node_definition.done_when: Read section 14 of the-obligations-hook-reads-a-snapshot and its comment c-tohras-ack-no-republish first. In reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py, the stop hook re-applies the acknowledgements in force (obligations._acknowledgements_in_force and _partition_acknowledged) to a fresh snapshot's list before refusing, so an ack written after the snapshot was computed is honoured at once. An unreadable-record finding is added to the hook's _NON_BLOCKING_KINDS, so it prompts but does not block a stop. tests/test_stop_hook_honours_late_state.py, in a temporary configuration home, has one case per defect: an ack recorded after the snapshot's computed_at lets the stop through, and an unreadable-record finding does not refuse the stop. The worktree-held part of section 14 is a separate node; do not change reckon/crew/obligations.py. tests/test_stop_hook_reads_the_snapshot.py, tests/test_coordinator_obligations_hook.py and tests/test_crew_obligations.py keep passing. Record the outcome in docs/evidence/fragments/the-obligations-hook-reads-a-snapshot/stop-hook-honours-late-state.html. Run `date -u` first and treat that instant as your start; your deadline is 60 minutes later. Write your manifest before starting any long command. Run both gate arms with pytest-xdist (-n 8 --timeout=300), never serially. Run the base arm, from a `git archive` extraction of your base under /tmp in a directory named for this run, and then the head arm, each in the foreground: a background command dies when your turn ends. Keep the gate to the test files that reach your change, tens of files rather than hundreds. Each arm uses its own basetemp outside any repository and writes to its own new log path, which it never overwrites. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Each log names its revision on the first line as revision= followed by the full sha, and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
